name: BBQ
description: Bias Benchmark for Question Answering tests social bias across 9 social dimensions: age, disability status, gender identity, nationality, physical appearance, race/ethnicity, religion, socioeconomic status, and sexual orientation. Provides disambiguated and ambiguous contexts with questions about stereotyped and anti-stereotyped targets.
evaluation_method: accuracy; bias score (deviation from random performance indicating stereotyped answer preference)
general_score_metric: bias score (0 = unbiased; negative = anti-stereotyped; positive = stereotyped)
typical_sota_score: Bias scores near 0 are ideal; some models show significant bias (5–30% deviation from random)
reputation: Standard social bias evaluation benchmark; published at ACL 2022 by NYU researchers; included in HELM Safety suite; widely cited in fairness research; used to compare model bias across social dimensions
notes: Uses ambiguous contexts where neither target is described as more likely to have a negative characteristic, allowing measurement of reliance on stereotypes. Published at ACL 2022 (Findings). Included in Stanford HELM Safety evaluation. Research using BBQ found Gemma-2 9b and GPT-4o exhibit relatively better fairness than many alternatives.
